objective: Audit only C17's fixed-placement corner bound through four explicit lemmas, Jordan-disk splicing and exact-coordinate adversarial arguments, without moving the drawing.

atomic_claims.text: Connected obstacle avoidance supplies one open free component and distinct nonedge-interior witnesses, even for boundary-only obstacle contact.
The eligible punctured-cell adjacency graph is connected without general position of supporting lines; witnesses on one-dimensional faces can be assigned to incident cells.
Pruning and finite line avoidance produce an embedded straight-line tree with E=2t-2+k and L=k for k>=2.
For N>=2, every open neighborhood of an embedded straight-line tree contains a filled simple polygon surrounding the tree with at most 2E+L corners, by explicit joints and interval splicing.
The four-lemma construction preserves the fixed drawing and yields at most max(3,2e^2-e+3*C(n,2)) corners, with k=0/1 handled by triangles.
All nine nonadjacent side pairs of the six-corner rational fixture are disjoint, and both complete tree segments lie in its interior by direct line equations and Jordan separation.

assumptions: Finite simple labeled graph with fixed injective real vertex coordinates; closed graph-edge segments and graph points form K.
A connected set avoiding K meets every nonedge; no openness, path connectedness or polygonality of that initial set is required.
Euclidean compactness, finite graph theory and the Jordan Polygon Theorem; all local joint and splicing premises are shown in the manuscript.
risks: This is a reviewable proof draft in the candidate-generation domain, not a trusted verifier receipt or admission.
No geometry script, SMT solver, grid program or proof assistant was executed; exact fixtures are displayed algebraic arguments.
The bound 2E+L excludes the one-vertex tree; L=k is used only after pruning and only for k>=2.
The drawing is never moved. C04/C07/C16 perturbation results, unrestricted one-obstacle completeness and the root remain outside this claim.
